merged_nodes.merged: 'the appearance of a peak at about 518 cm-1 ... corresponds to the TO mode of crystalline silicon' and 'this indicates the formation of silicon crystalline grains in the film' and 'the deviation of the position from 520 cm-1 is associated with the finite small sizes of crystal grains'
merged_nodes.why: three sentences of the F2 linked text state one phase-identity claim; the grain-size reading of the peak position is the KNW lookup k1, not a second claim

merged_nodes.merged: 'partial removal of the material occurs at the center of the irradiated area resulting in the donut-like shape' (F3 linked text, SEM) and 'the depths of the laser annealed spots are 97 +/- 13 nm (FaS) and 94 +/- 16 nm (LuS); the widths are 494 +/- 100 and 488 +/- 90 nm' (F4 linked text, AFM)
merged_nodes.why: one crater-geometry claim read from two instruments; SEM gives the shape, AFM the depth and width, and the paper uses them for the same point, that the two spot types look the same

merged_nodes.merged: 'the increase in the laser processing fluence leads to the growth of the amplitude for the PL signal' and 'the reason for the subsequent decrease of the PL signal is the evaporation of the material when the laser intensity exceeds the damage threshold'
merged_nodes.why: rise and fall are one non-monotonic trend of the same property against the same variable; the evaporation reading is the separate mechanism node m3

merged_nodes.merged: 'such treatment has no influence on the label photoluminescent properties' and 'since the erbium layer was removed, spots recorded at the fourth step are non-luminescent but look like LuS'
merged_nodes.why: both are the one property claim that F4c shows as two traces: the luminescent spots survive the etch and the spots written after it do not emit
